Legacy campaign

Affordable Growth (1922–1941)

Your California utility has more customers now. They need enough new capacity to meet rising demand, at a rate they can still afford.

Open the Legacy campaign↗ Your decisions ↓

Play the chapters in order. You carry the same utility from one generation to the next.

Location
A fictional California utility
Starts in
1922
Generation
20 years

Your starting point

In 1922 you take over the company you built in Beyond the Dynamo. The plants have aged another twenty years, and any debt you've taken on still needs to be paid.

At the end of 1941, the campaign checks the rate you actually billed your customers. Check the target before you decide how much to spend on construction.

Learn how to play

Your decisions

  1. 01

    Compare the running costs

    Look at what a new project's fuel and upkeep would add to each bill, alongside the cost to build it.

  2. 02

    Decide how much to borrow

    If new capacity opens too soon, you're paying for equipment that sits idle. Check the demand forecast before committing to a loan.

  3. 03

    Set the rate

    Compare the target with what you're charging. Can you afford the next round of construction at that rate?

What would your customers pay for a kilowatt-hour in 1941?
